This one is not as good as everyone says.
The protagonist is boring and lifeless, and I guessed the twist ending ten minutes in. The writing is competent but uninspiring. There really is nothing in the story department that you haven't seen before.
Gameplay is repetitious. You'll spend a lot of time backtracking through the same samey areas over and over. Your character is in constant need of rest or food, which is more annoying than compelling. The food crafting system is bizarrely over-complex, and entails a lot of time spent struggling with the terrible interface. Speaking of...
Controls are baffling laid-out. Presumably this is meant to make combat more stressful and convey that our character is not some bad♥♥♥♥♥super soldier, but in reality it just means looking away from the game at your keyboard to realign your fingers every time you need to do anything other than walk and look at stuff. The hotkeys are a total joke.
If you get it as part of a bundle, it might be worth your time to try it out, but I cannot recommend buying this game.

An amazing horror game with a brilliant atmosphere that comes from a combination of a killer soundtrack, distorted pixel graphics, and themes from classic games of the genre. As a role-playing game, there are many unforeseen consequences that can come of each of your actions. The game can feel a little short, with maybe 2-5 hours per run, but with the multiple  possible endings and different high scores, it has a lot of replay value. This is the developer's best work yet; it's definitely worth picking up. TL;DR: needs Steam Achievements.

While not being the scariest horror game out there, Lone Survivor delivers an interesting story and enviorment. While the 2D gameplay feels a bit strange at first, after a while it all feels like it fits. The game itself is relatively short, it can easily be completed within 3-6 hours even if you go into it without any idea what you're doing. Though it's a very interesting game in itself, it has a few drawbacks. At regular intervals your character will constantly need food and rest, trying to attend to these needs can get frustrating at times. While the story and cutscenes are all interesting they are painfully cryptic, constantly leaving you guessing at what is happening. There are multiple endings, but two of them are nearly idendical, and getting the best ending is most likely impossible without some kind of walkthrough, as the hints to what you need to do in order to obtain those endings are extremly subtle. All in all, I think the experience is worth the price tag.
Pros:
+The 8-bit graphics are very well-made
+Gameplay is unique
+Multiple paths and endings
+The enviroment and Story are eerie, disturbing, and interesting
+Great Soundtrack
Cons:
-If you're looking for a super-intense horror experience, you may want to look elsewhere
-Your character can be too needy
-Story is cryptic
-Getting better endings may require a walkthrough

It is full of intrigue, mystery, subtlety and suspense.  I prefer this type of horror to the in-your-face style of Dead Space or similar titles.  You should play this alone, and in the dark. Absolutely beautiful game with really "meaty" combat animations! Surprisingly intreresting combat once you get past level 6 or so. There are plenty of interesting synergies between your characters, and I really like the mana-managment. Another thing that lifts the combat encounters: Enemies are smart enough to be a challenge, and have a variety of attacks to throw at you, especially if you do dungeons on higher difficulties.
I only had one instane where I had to restart the game, I managed to trigger a dialogue at the same time as a combat encounter and could therefore proceed with neither, but the autosave got me back to the same place in less than a minute so no big deal.

I`m 313 hours into Stellaris.  I haven´t completed it, but I believe I can give a pretty good impression of the game.
This review includes ALL the DLCs, up to and including Utopia.
Stellaris is one of those unique games where random♥♥♥♥♥♥happens so often that one game can feel like several new playthroughs. Over 300 hours into the game, I still often find brand new things happening  in single player and multiplayer modes.
You start with a single planet and a few people.  From there, you go off to take over the universe. You will encounter everything from space dragons, horrors of the void and pirates that will try to kill you. For that matter, half of the universe will also attempt to kill or devour you. The rest wanna make friends or simply breed you out of history.
Going into Stellaris, it is important to know that this is NOT a game you will finish in a day or a week.  It's a game where you should take your time and really learn and understand what is going on. It´s a game where every choice you make for your population affects the outcome of the game.
Reasearch, building, military and social aspects of your population are by your command. There are a million tools to reach your goal, so you get to pick whatever you want.
You wanna be a insane warmonger ? Sure, go ahead,
You wanna be a spiritual leader who believes in peace ? Sure, go ahead.
You wanna be the most tech-savvy scientist and have every population below you ? Sure, go ahead.
You wish to enslave the entire world and feel like a king with slaves ? Sure, go ahead.
You wanna be a complete asshat and purge people who disagree with you ? Sure, go ahead.
Stellaris lets you truly customize according to your whims and rule the universe as you like, which is great.
Design your own race, from appearance to values.
Design your own ships, with weapons, shields, and FTL drives.
Design your own planets with terraforming and much more.
Gameplay and graphics are amazing, complemented by a soundtrack that promotes relaxation on your journey into space.
Stellaris is strongly recommended for people who love complex, long-running GRTS games.
One of the best strategy games I have played in a long while. Worth picking up.

I did not know anything of 4X genre before I played this game. Of course I had tried Civilization IV but the turnbased style did not appeal to me. All in all I found the game a little cartoonish. In 2010 I bought Europa Universalis 3 when it was on sale. A friend abroad said it was good. I actually did not know anyhting of the game and when I started it nothing was understandable. The game was uninstalled and put in a locker. Fast forward some years and about 2013 I saw that Europa Universalis 4 was on sale here. I bought it with all DLC`s. Again I did not understand a thing. It is funny to think that I even did not complete the tutorial. I was stuck in Essex! But with a little bit of endeavour I learnt a lot by reading wikis, watch Lets play videos on YouTube and talk to people on Paradox forums. I have about 349 hours played and I love it!!!
Since I got this admiration for Paradox Interactive it was reasonable to look to their other games. Among many Stellaris captured my attention. Like most Paradox games the learning curve is steep. But this time they have listened to the fans and implemented a good tutor ingame. They have also made room for modders and right there are many mods to select made by players. I myself have made plenty of music mods and I am not even a programmer! But the game engages so much and I learn practically new things every day.
At the start of the game you can choose between several different species with their unique ethos, tradition, government type and so on. Here you can also customize a lot and make something you like. In the game details screen you can choose among many thing clustered or random placed empires. Do you want some species to be advanced at the start? Do you prefer the same FTL (Faster Than Light) technology for all players or can they have their own? Do you want end crisis? All these options are available in the game details screen. When you start the game you get the option to have full tutorial, partial or off. This is very good option for newbies. You start in your system and start surveying and so on. You are in action!
The visuals are stunning and mouthwatering. Their are plenty of mods which make the experience even better. The UI (User Interface) is easy to learn and after some practice it is very good to use. But I recommend installing a UI overhauls mod which makes thing even more systematic and easy to find. If you want to use hotkeys they are in place. Battles or a joy to experience but you may want to reduce the blooming effect.
Sound is good as it is in all Paradox games. The official soundtrack is beautiful and if you want more music, take a look in the modding community on Steam for the game. There are many good and excellents mods to choose between. Another good thing Paradox did was to implement a music player in the game so you actually see the tracks. They did the same in Europa Universalis 4. Clearly a forward looking company, Paradox.
At this moment the game is very rich on content early on and in the middle but the last part is rather emptier. So you basically just go to galaxy map and see how things are going. But as we know Partadox games tend to be better and better as time goes because they are sincerely engaged in their products. So we can expect thing to change in the coming time. They have already released some patches and DLC`s and a new patch is coming next week. Of course you can subscribe to content mods and get more flavour in the game.
I highly recommend this game and give it 10/10. Never has a game engaged me so much. I dream of it, think of it and engage a lot. I am sure you will have the same experience. It will surely be supported in the years to come. My personal opinion is that it surpasses many titles in this genre. A huge plus is also the modding community which are creative and innovative.

I'm going to give my best attempts at writing a solid review, bear with me.
I found this game via a let's play on Youtube. I wasn't expecting much, but as soon as I saw the graphical style, I was really interested. It looked like something out of Ratchet and Clank and possibly even designed by Blizzard. I didn't finish the video because I wanted to experience the game myself, and I'm sure glad I did....
Going into the game, I didn't expect much in terms of the character customization, the class selection, and the path selection was really unexpected. I really enjoyed the opening sequence of the game and it really gave you an idea of the kind of humor and overall action you're going to expect from the game.
Selecting a character and creating one took me over half an hour because I was extremely un desicive but that's just me, but it does usually mean I've got a good game on my hands. I'm a little disappointed that this game has some bad reviews because I've honestly fallen completely in love with it.
It's not pay to win, you can get mounts and pets without the store needed. The only downside is that if you want to unlock another character slot you'll have to either purchase one with microtransactions or omnibits. Omnibits are great, and aren't actually that hard to get, unless you're saving for a bigger purchase, that might take a while.
The combat system in this game is a lot of fun, I enjoy aiming, dodging and generally not feeling like I'm just pressing a button without thinking.
The community is sadly quite small. While this has its benefits, it makes for finding parties/groups to do dungeons in quite difficult. But the game has an auto queue system to help group people together in order to do this, and if you find yourself waiting for far too long, simply hop onto the zone chat and someone will most likely help you out. And they'll help you out for more than just the dungeons!
I'd recommend trying this game for yourself, giving it a good few hours, and not to expect anything. This is an MMO, and it's a great one at that. The fact that this is free just makes it a whole lot better.

I've had this game highly reccommended and had been told it was one of those hidden gems on steam that I just had to play through if I wanted good horror. After finally playing through it, I was disappointed on most of those accounts.
What it does right: For what could be a gameboy  game, it certainly has a decent atmosphere and mechanics that I couldn't complain about, even with the menu system. It was interesting enough that I wanted to see what happened next and I actually finished it, but not enough to want to play through it again or try to find out the smaller details of the plot.
What it does wrong: For a game that had been paraded to me for how scary it was, it really wasn't. The few first experiences with the thin men were creepy, especially if I ran out of ammo, but the fact that you have a limitless supply of ammo and batteries if you take pills takes any stress out of the game. There's no suspense if I can just walk up, shoot the things in the head a few times and be done with it. Coupled with the fact that I could go home and save somewhere within every level at any time, things just weren't tense or suspenseful enough to make me feell actually afraid or in the moment. It became more strategical as the game went on, instead of me being actually afraid. I suppose it would be hard to really set up a realistic experience with the size of the game, but I'm sure it could've been done better.
Like I said, having an unlimited supply to pills, and therefore and unlimited supply of ammo and batteries takes a lot of what could be a good survival element out of the game.  When I initially found out you could do this, I stopped trying to avoid the monsters entirely. Why take the time to avoid the problem every time you go through that area if you can permanantly remove it? It might've been different if my ammo supply was actually limited. Any fear of these monsters was entirely gone when I figured out it was that easy to take them down.
Another thing was the protagonists messages. They seem entirely useless after a while. While initially he complains about hunger or sleep, when he starts saying he might collapse and other things, I would try to eat or sleep to no avail. It seems that message system wasn't entirely necessary, and I just ignored it entirely when I would eat and sleep at regular intervals. Maybe it had something to do with his gradual downward descent, but it certainly wasn't helpful from a gameplay standpoint.
Lastly, I hesitate to call it something that was done wrong, but the story. [ALSO SPOILERS] I see it was trying to be this deep journey about a guy imagining his own depressing world after his girlfriend was killed in a car crash or something, but it never took the time to make me interested in the main character or his situation enough to really care for him. This may be to try to immerse the player deeper into the role, but that never works when you're trying to tell a compelling story at the same time. It may just be me, but the story was never involving enough to make me like the game any more than I already did.
It was also really short, but I guess that isn't a bad thing. I could've beat it in two or three hours if I didn't mess around so much.
Guess it was an alright experience, but I doubt I'll ever come back to it. Dunno if I would've actually paid fifteen dollars for it if I'd known what it was really going to be.

I really knew next to nothing about the game when I started. I had only read a few lines of positive feedback on it, and seen about 5 minutes of gameplay on youtube, after which it had captured my interest enough for me to take a chance on it, and I'm thoroughly glad I did. It turned out to be one of the best indie titles I've played. The reason for this is perhaps because I went in blind with no real prior knowledge or spoilers about the game. There's something to be said for experiencing a game in this manner. I thoroughly recommend it.
As for the story.. Well it's rather hard to talk too much about the story in detail. Partly because it's fairly weird (no, really), and partly because there isn't much of a story at all. It's one of those kind of games where the whole world has gone mad, you are seemingly one of the very few survivors of what must have been an event that ended civilization.
You wake up in your apartment, which acts as your safe zone, where you can sleep (save), and prepare food and drink, and other things. Once you venture outside, you quickly find out that in order to survive, you have to deal with the monsters that now roam the halls and inhabit the other apartments.
One way to deal with them is to shoot them with your trusty pistol, though you can't just go all gung ho, because if you run out of ammo, you're in for a rough time since there are no other weapons in the game. However, there are various ways of getting more ammo along the way, so it's not the end of the world. I ran out of ammo once, and it took me quite a while to get more, but in the meantime I took the more stealthy approach, which is absolutely viable, and perhaps even preferable for large parts of the game.
The controls are a bit clunky if things have to go fast in terms of inventory management while monsters are about. The reason for this is that there is no way of stopping time. It'll just keep ticking away regardless of what you're doing, which means monsters aren't going to stand around and wait for you to open your inventory, find the right item, and use it. They will just make short work if you while you are otherwise occupied with your inventory.
This is a good thing though, as having time stop just because you want to open up your inventory and find items in the middle of combat really breaks the immersion, so be prepared to run away to a "safe" area before taking care of your health or mental state.
Speaking of inventory management, you will often find that you get hungry or tired as you explore the game, and since you can die of both starvation and exhaustion in this game, you'll always have to be aware of how much food and drink  you have on you, and how much time it'll take you to get back to your apartment in order to sleep in case you don't have caffeine on you. You can even die if you run out of batteries for your flashlight, so you have to watch out how much you have it turned on.
Speaking of food. You might not always have the right equipment in your kitchen to cook what you find along the way either, so you'll also need to find the proper cookware if you want to prepare the various foods in the game. Apparently, you were a big fan of ordering in before the world turned bad, because you don't seem to own much of anything in that department.
The game took me a little under 5 hours to complete, and I really enjoyed every moment of it. I imagine this is much like what the original Silent Hill would have been like if they had gone with a 2-d side scroller instead of 3d.
It's well worth your time and money, so I say go for it if you're a fan of the genre. You won't regret it.

First, World of Planes was made irrelavent by Warthuder. Then Warthunder added tank combat which eclipsed the 'World of X' crap Wargaming pumped out. Now this, I would argue, is the last nail in their coffin. Especially since the developers of this, unlike both World of Whatever and War Thunder, actually bother to balance the tiers based on how effective a ship is rather than listing them arbitrarily by when they were made.
The controls are very straight forward and the mechanics don't hold your hand too much. Its also free to play so, I'd have to call you an idiot for not at least trying this game, if you have any interest in naval combat that is.

It's like WoWS with ♥♥♥♥♥ier graphics and framerate. Includes submarines, went about as well as I expected.
Pretty much it's NavyField in 3D. If you like that, then you will probably enjoy this. If you have a 4gb graphics card, then you can expect to get 50FPS on certain maps and 5 on others. Needs a huge amount of optimising.
In addition, Aircraft Carriers are horribly balanced. They get shot down in half a second, their bombs do very little damage, and there are EXTREMELY limited controls for them. There is no grouping options, carriers have very delicate planes, to some of you this seems like heaven because they can't do anything, but to others this is a horrific balance. Essentially AA is WAY too effective, a single destroyer can swat off a squad of 9 dive bombers, and take no damage. Cruisers, Carriers, Battleships, good luck. You are going to need it. Tier 2s will obliterate entire waves in seconds, a group of people and you might as well just rush in and try to use main batteries.
Submarines are also unbalanced. The only thing in the game capable of hurting them is a Destroyer, which have god awful guns. The range of their torpedoes are long enough where they don't have to be in the front lines, they can sit in the back while the other team is totally helpless to do ANYTHING to stop them.
There are no servers for people other than North America. I live in NA, so the ping wouldn't be an issue... Right? Nah, 300+ ping spikes every few seconds. Internet isn't the issue here, friend is having it as well. Lots of people complaining about it in game.
Community is bad, people TK each other constantly with Torpedoes, whether they wanted to or if they are just totally brain dead I don't know, but every game there are 6+ blue people(People who have consistently team killed). Teams themselves are either a winning team or a losing team, there are no close battles. Chat is worse, languages you can't understand because the people have nowhere to go, again because of the servers.
There is a pay to win system in place. Gold ammo, does more damage and more penetration, costs ONLY gold(You buy this with money ONLY.) UI is confusing, new players don't understand mechanics. Tutorial explains very little, doesn't explain that there is no such thing as a friendly torpedo. Doesn't ever explain the actual ship UI.
Honestly, game has potential. But it's laggy in terms of FPS, laggy in terms of Ping, has no servers for anyone outside NA, haven't seen any moderation at all, Pay to Win already in place, Balance issues galore... It needs a lot of work. Til then, just wait and watch. Or play, it is a Free to play* game.
*unless you want to do more damage and penetration.

In the state the game is now I cannot recommend it.
If you like arcade action, it may be something you want to look at, but keep in mind:
* The graphics are shoddy and blurry, so much so as it detracts from the game

* Even more arcady than the competitor World of warships

The game feels like... you know those chinese carboncopy knockoffs? Like the "BMW but not really BMW"-car (Brilliance V5) and the "Landcruiser but not Landcruiser" (LandWind)?
The feeling of the game is like that; the quality is a bit... questionable, and the game is abit... wonky and awkward at places. Its not World of Tanks/Warships... but it is kindof... like the hillbilly cousin version of it.

Edit; return 1 year and 1 month later.
Can I recommend the game in its current state?
Yes, its has gotten a lot better in a year, and its free, so try it out.
Returning to my last points:
* Graphics: Not as shoddy/blurry as last time. It doesnt detract from the game-experience any longer, and it is passable.
* Performance; no crashes nor choppiness.
* Arcadiness; yup, still there. Its the design of the game so...
* Still feels like WoT on the ocean, however this is not a problem anylonger. It feels more polished.
The game still has that chinese knockoff copy feel to it, but its maturing into its own game. The UI is still bad, the graphics arent the most fanciest out there (but it isnt downright an eyesore anymore), the wonkyness is still there but has gone into more of quirks of the game instead of feeling like a bad thing.
TL:DR It still feels like a wannabe copy of the leading competitor World of warships/tanks but it is maturing nicely and still has a lot of potential. Try it out, its free after all.

I do not know what I can say about this game, other than it being a masterpiece. I have to say that this is one of the best games I have ever played. Everything in it was just so good: the gameplay, the story and the setting, the characters etc, but the game did have some performance issues.
All of the characters were crafted pretty well but they did have some certain noticeable tropes, for example: 2B is the serious character while 9S is a more childish and loose character, even though these tropes were so obvious the characters were still pretty interesting and built up pretty well throughout the story. There are some characters which seem like they are made for comedic relief but really have a deep side story, example (Emil). Overall the characters in this game were great
The story in this game is amazing, it has a series of really unexpected plot twists and amazing moments that I will remember for a long time. I think that the setting for this game was also a bit radical being a set a very long time in the future with androids everywhere and a giant space station, but on the ground everything seemed pretty old which was a pretty weird design decision and I liked it, this whole artstyle actually tied in with the old games so there was a good reason to choose such a different look for the game. The whole backstory of this game was also pretty amazing, you didn't really need to play the old games to get the main part of the story but if you wanted to go deeper and find out more you would have to refer to the old games like Nier: Gestalt. To be honest I found myself to be really invested in the storyline as it was pretty different from anything I have played.
There are some really nice and original gameplay mechanics in it as well like being able to take off your HUD to make space for upgrades, the whole upgrade system in the game was really interesting and well crafted, I think that it was a very good choice to experiment with it and not make the upgrade system as basic as skill points, the upgrade system could also help you find entirely new moves which was pretty cool. The weapon upgrade system was pretty simple which isn't a bad thing, it didn't need to be any harder. The fighting in the game wasn't that satisfying but it was fine, the actual moves that you can do were at first pretty basic with only having a heavy and a light attack but as you play and combine the moves together you can find some combos that the game did not tell you about. I think that one good choice in this game was how you could equip the weapons because it forced you to think about what do you want on the heavy attack and on the light attack, do you want a small sword with a heavy attack, or a large sword with a heavy attack? There was also quite a lot of weapons that you could find around the world and buy from stores which would benefit you a lot as you go on.
The performance issues did not even bother me since I was so invested into the game and they really weren't that bad, the only big problem that happened to me was 30fps lock on cutscenes (disgusting) and the low fps ingame. Having a pretty beefy computer I would expect this game to run better, but for me it wasn't really that big of a problem.
To summarise this game, I have to say that is very well made with a good story, characters, setting and gameplay elements, but this game was limited by it's performance issues. Overall this game was really one of the best games I have ever played and an actual masterpiece. This was definitely one of the best games I have ever played on one of the best games of 2017. I would have to give this game at least a 9/10 and to quote Jim Sterling - "I history forgets this game, then ♥♥♥♥ history."

Within 3 days this game made me spend 40.5 hours of my life on it. That is when you know this game has something good in it.
Scroll down to the bottom for a TL:DR.
As you start playing the game there will be a lot of confusions and a lot of buttons to press, but do not worry, you'll get the hang of it rather soon, since the tutorial helps pretty well.
After you've learned to play the game, there is a rather big universe for you to explore, ranging from 200 to 1000 systems. However, you won't be the only one doing so. There are other factions(dependent on how many you set) to compete with you on that subject. You will have to put a lot of effort and investments into expanding your territory.
As you will be exploring, you'll see a vast amount of options and paths for you to go, as it is for the direction of expanding your territory, so is it for a lot of other things, such as researching, politics(and things related to them), etc.
As an addition to all of the things above, everything in this game works smooth like butter, including multiplayer, and there is also customization for the faction&race that you play and ships that you'll use in the game, a lot unlike in many other games. Plus the Workshop integration allows you to easily download the crapload of community-made content. (don't forget to enable it in the launcher afterwards)
All in all, it is a great game that makes a good change to the things you see on the market nowadays. Personally for me, it is rather masterpieceful compared to them.

Alright, let's talk a bit about Loadout.
Loadout, for those not in the know, is a third person shooter developed by Edge of Reality. And the name of the company is an accurate description of this game.
As I said, Loadout IS another third person shooter, but it has STUPID amounts of weapon customization. Example: I have a laser rifle. I can mount a scope on it, give it a sniper barrel, semi-auto trigger, and BAM. Instant laser sniper rifle. Or say I have a rocket launcher. Add a camera on to the projectiles to guide them, manual detonation, and BAM. Instant Valkyrie Rockets.
With that said, is the weapon customization a good thing? Yes and no.
Yes, because it allows the player to personalize their own weapon to fit their playstyles. No, because people will find STUPID exploits with the weapons. And they will use them. Hopefully, there will be balance issues that are sorted out VERY soon.
In the end, Loadout is silly, but I do enjoy it for what it is. And it's free, with one of the best business models on the market today. 8/10.

Although Medieval II TW seems like an expansion of Rome TW, with slightly better graphics, more factions (when including the Medieval II TW expansions), it is def worth the relatively cheap Steam price. Although Medieval II TW It does not play like an entirely different game (unlike Empire TW and Napoleon TW since they have guns), the feel is still different given the different time period and the respective time period specific relationships between different countries. Medieval TW is mostly made from the same formula as Rome TW, but it tells completely different stories, keeping the game from feeling like a simple reiteration of Rome TW.  Furthermore, mods like Third Age and Elder Scrolls further increase the replayability and overall value of this game.

If you want the definitive Total War experience Medieval 2 is it. Unlike new Total War games, Medieval 2 is much more complex in its gameplay mechanics. From maintaining merchants and diplomats to army management. Medieval 2 feels more of an empire building simulator than newer games such as Rome 2.
Battles feel much heavier and units tend to react more realistically to commands. The sense of weight makes battle feel much more organic than Shogun 2, Rome 2 or even Fantasy Warhammer.
If you do choose to buy this game, be sure to install Stainless Steel as it provides a much more historical early and late game era campaign. You can check out some footage of it on my YouTube channel.

Having played this since the original release and recently rebought it on steam, it is still absolutely worth the money and one of the best total war games ever made.
Combining a blend of economic advancement, diplomatic shenanigans and military conquest, you definetely have room to manouvre with how you play with your faction, whatever your playstyle.
Yes, there are some issues, such as ridiculously OP cavalry charges, scarily buggy battles on mountain terrain-style maps (some units are literally stuck and unreachable), and the AI's diplomatic nature completely unfathomable and changing (Always fun declaring war on the Papal States, conquering Rome then declaring a ceasefire by buying them off and then electing the new pope next turn with your legion of cardinals).
However, these are miniscual when compared to how many hours you can plug away into this game and still really enjoy it, especially when you only begin to the tap into the mods that are available (Third age total war, Skyrim, Westeros e.t.c.).

This game has been in my Steam Inventory for a very, very long time. I was unsure if I really wanted to activate it or maybe try to sell for a few Cents. When I realized that nobody would buy it as a Steam gift, I just went what the heck and activated it.
What a mistake.
To start with, the Steam page has to be one of the most misleading things I've ever seen. There's only one screenshot with text on it, the rest showing environment. It gave me the impression of a very atmospheric game with the world telling its story. That's not the case. This story is like reading a book, only with a little spherical music and broken flashlights.
When the game ended I still didn't know what the hell was going on, partly because I just couldn't be bothered to continue reading every little block of text that was dumped at my feet. Write a book if that's what you feel like, don't put a few quotes into a game and call it a day.
From what I got, the story goes along the lines of four people being stranded on an island, and then there is an argument, and then everybody except the player dies. You apparently have a concussion and forget everything, then you wake up in a dark room (game starts here). You piece together the "story" by constantly clicking everything that makes a symbol appear on your crosshair. Soon you realize you don't know what the hell to do, even after you think you saw everything. There's a mountain you can't enter until night, and even as the day progresses you can't (there should've been a definition of it, like "Night means it's dark as ♥♥♥♥", so I wouldn't have to waste so much time running back and forth). Some blah happens that I really can't care about to explain, but it involves an pointlessly gloomy room (first screenshot on the Steam page), claiming that "The Moon Sliver was gone". Wowee. Some thing that we don't care about or haven't been introduced to yet is missing. The punchline, please?
To cut a long story short (well, it already is short as hell, about an hour), you go into the mountain, a long corridor with no doors, end up at a desk with a book and a candle, all the while reading some thing about a girl killing herself for some stupid reason. Then you turn around and some black humanoid Slenderman-esque model appears behind you, the game turns to black, and the credits roll. Well, not roll. You literally walk through the credits (one of the few aspects I actually original enough to like it). But there's no end. You just walk and walk until you hit an invisible box, up until you realize you're trapped in a giant cuboid. Is there some deeper meaning to this or was the developer just too lazy to add something to go back to the main menu?
I could go on rambling about the lack of artistic skills, because the game relies way too much on fog to hide its terrible modeling qualities. The water, for example, looks like clipping plastic if anything. However, just the horrible "story" aspects should already give you enough of a picture. Plus, I really can't be bothered to.
Now, what is it that this game did so much worse than Dear Esther, which, despite having the same general interactive-story-on-a-lonesome-island concept, was a really enjoyable game? To reduce it to a single word:
.
With a proper narration instead of text snippets that the player stops caring about two minutes into the game, this could actually have been interesting. The story fragments that I could be arsed to pick up were at least somewhat interesting. But the delivery was missing, as, by the time the game was finished, I was barely into it. I already forgot the names of the characters, or the reason why I was on that island, or why some dude just randomly appeared behind me at the end. It just relies way too much on the player giving a damn for things he clearly doesn't.
As it stands, all that remains when you put aside these aspects is a very sour taste and the itch in my fingers to somehow pull out the two bucks I wasted on this game and get a cheeseburger for them or something.

JRPG style Roleplaying done with a very western comic book flair, and done very well.
I was amazed that this game could carry over the comic book aesthetic of it's source material into a video game so well.  While I admittedly knew nothing of the comics before playing, this game made me want to go out and read them and learn more about the vibrant characters and world that the game is set in.  Further, while no knowledge is needed from the comics to enjoy the game, I'm told that the two are set at different times so there's also no need to worry about spoilers, which is nice.
The gameplay is smooth and the combats are handled well, with only a few hiccups when it comes to the power curve in the game.  One of the truly interesting things is how the characters and their powers play off each other.  What one person might consider 'the best group' may be someone elses worst.  Or may not even be good in certain situations.  It encourages exploration of the roles.  Unfortunately this brings to light the biggest flaw in the game.  Each character earns exp individually and independantly.  Don't use a guy for a dungeon or two?  Have fun grinding to get his exp up to everyone else's level.  Trust me, this also offsets the other problem in the game.  One or two levels makes a huge difference.  Especially as the gear is often 'teired' every 3 levels or so.  Going into a dungeon where you're a level below, and your gear is maybe 4-6 levels below is just not going to work out very well for you.  But this can be fixed with grinding and is really the only major downside to the game in my opinion.  The music is top notch as are the sound effects and the voice acting.  Overall, as a fan of RPG games I highly reccomend this one.
Pros:
- beautiful game on every level
- solid game play and combat
- interesting characters / story
- deep game play through
- interesting crafting system that feels optional but powerful
- lots of little secrets to increase replayability of dungeons
Cons:
- Party doesn't share EXP, leading to VAST gulfs in experience levels
- Can be very grindy to get characters to the required power for next dungeon
- Resources (gold, crafting, loot, etc) feels very sparse, which again can lead to grindyness
I highly suggest this game is worth your money if you like RPGs and don't mind a bit of a grind at times through already cleared content.  You won't regret it.

This is not a bad game at all. If you enjoyed playing Battlestations Pacific or Navyfield, then you should be right at home with this game.
First off the cons:
The UI is clunky. Let's face it, there are just a huge amount of tabs to sort through and when you are playing carriers there is no way to group together aircraft or zoom out the map and give pathing orders.  Also, when you are firing your cannons in the traditional scoped view, you have to constantly adjust and readjust with jerky camera movements. The lack of gun plane stabilization like that which is present in World of Warships (x key) is annoying but really hurts destroyers and cruisers.
Average graphics. World of Warships (the main game that this will be compared to) definitely has better visual fidelity. The models are not exactly to scale which is sometimes jarring but this is more than made up for by the vast features Steel Ocean brings to the table.
Poor optimization. I play on laptop with an i5-5200u and HD5500 igpu and I just barely get 30fps (mostly around 20fps) with the settings on low. World of warships always stays above 30fps in the 40s however with all the torpedo particles and gunfire effects there is probably good reason for the slowdown. Especially torpedoes, I get frame drops when I use those.
Low tier balance issues. Playing cruisers at low tiers will give you an awful grind. You will get pounded from long range by battleships that out-range you by quite a bit. Also Battleships tend to keep in the back of the map so you will have to go through the front line of submarines to get them.
Now for the pros:
Submarines! The main selling point of the game, you can submerge and surface to avoid gunfire however with a large penalty to movement speed. Subs are very fragile but if you can sneak up on a carrier or battleship, you will definitely rebalance them. There are two dive states; shallow depth and crash depth. At shallow depth you can still fire your torpedoes and your oxygen (time allowed to stay submerged) will depleted slowly. You are still vulnerable to air and ship launched torpedos as well as depth charges. At crash depth nothing will be able to hit you except depth charges, so use this to dodge torpedos and try to stay clear of cruisers and destroyers.
Each class of ship has a clear defined role. Like rock, paper, scissors, Steel Ocean has multiple classes of ships that are very effective against each other. Battleships will tear up cruisers like butter from long-range, while submarines prowl the seas for that lone BB and send him to Davey Jones Locker. Destroyers are fast and maneuverable with lots of torpedoes, high sonar capabilities, and depth charges(anti-sub). Cruisers are bigger and better armed than destroyers but are less maneuverable and have more of a difficult time landing depth charges on subs(anti-DD). Carriers are the jack of all trades, they can effectively sink shallow depth submarines and pose a large threat to battleships. Carriers are limited by a poor UI however, and you can only assign a maximum of 5 planes in one air group (you get multiple air groups). Manual AA fire is also very effective against planes.
You can control your secondary armament and AA fire! Are you tired of playing a horrible underpowered Kawachi with useless secondaries in World of Warships? Fear not! You can control all 14 of those devastating 152mm sponsoon guns and seriously harm any marauding destroyers. Dislike those scouts or fighter planes lighting up your position? Open fire with all guns blazing and shoot down those planes knowing that it is your aiming skill and not the ai doing the work!
Steel Oceans has great potential as a Battlestations/Navyfield hybrid and could pose a threat to WoWs with proper optimization and a UI overhaul. Proper team play is very effective with designated roles, however like your average tomato WOT or WoWs player, you will not see coordination that often. Hunting for subs and battleships in submarine wolfpack is great fun and it is incredibly satisfying to know that those torpedoes you launched were from your skill alone. (NO aim assist for torpedoes) With time I think this game will truly start to shine, it just needs a bit of polish.

There are next to no jumpscares in this game. With that said, there shouldn't be any hesitation about entering the dark corridors.
And yet, it's still one of the most terrifying things I've ever played.
You'll always know where the hazards are. You'll always know how badly things will go if you make a mistake. You'll always have more than enough time to let the dread settle in as you step out into the next area only to find that things have gone much darker, and the infected are practically everywhere.
This isn't a game that is meant to make you rush things. You'll revisit areas over a course of several in-game days, having to ration your food and knowing when to sleep, and figuring out how to slow your descent into madness.
If you're rushing things, it probably means that you're panicking. But you might be doing a lot of that.

Got this game back in June 2012, but didn't get around to playing it until now. And wow - Lone Survivor is a wonderful game by the obviously talented Jasper Byrne. With it's surreal Twin Peaks meets Silent Hill feeling it manages to weave together elements from many genres. The gameplay of the survival horror genre, the look of old school adventure games, the intelligence and introspection of other new indie games, and some pretty funny and seriously dark humor, Lone Survivor is best describes as a survival horror game though, and while it doesn't scare you it may very well haunt you in different ways. It's a moving game with more than a small touch of emotion and the bizarre, and it's a game I should have played a long time ago. It's also a game anyone can pick up. It doesn't really require any skills or knowledge of a specific genre to appreciate.
If you're wondering if you should pick it up? The answer is simple: "Yes! Yes, you should pick it up! NOW!" While a playthough won't take more than between 3-6 hours (depending on playstyle and the amount of exploring you do), the game (especially the director's cut) should be played at least 2-3 times. There are five different endings and, while it may not look like it, the game is extremely detailed. Every action has consequences, but they are far from apparent. Lone Survivor is not just an interesting and beautiful game, it's a damn good one with great gameplay. This is a game that quickly rose to my top-20 list of best games of all time. A definite must have.
Even now, in 2017, I'm still waiting for a sequel. Waiting for anyone to expand on what Byrne created. This is one of the best games on Steam and I just wanna wipe my memory and play it again.

In the deserts you have to deal with a sandstorm that limits visibility or the bright lit city has a higher visibility than normal requiring you to move from cover to cover than to be reliant on your stealth camo. The actual gameplay is what you would expect. At its surface its a average third person shooter. Cover system, shoot from cover ect. But what changes it is the missions and gear you get.
Right out the gate you can tackle almost every mission either stealth or loud. With some exceptions where it does force you to one playstyle for story purposes. Both playstyles have their own pros and cons. Stealth: Leave guards be but if you mess up they will be reinforcments and make you goal alot harder and usually leaves you in a bad position. Loud: Dead guys cant hurt you but engaging with them it tough requring you to thin the ranks out and sabatoge vehicles before engaging.
Gun customization is the best its been. Really choose what you want your gun to look like as well as more importantly perform like. You can change a semi-automatic shotgun into a long range fully automatic shotgun that shoots fire rounds. Yeah its freaking sweet. Gadgets are just as diverse.
The AI is solid. They actually help in firefights and the ability to do a 4 person squad takedown at the same time not only so good at clearing at but also sweet. It never felt overpowered as you have to tag them and that usually meant getting close to them on foot to mark them or using your UAV which left you in a vunerable position. Choices. The levels are linear with some open areas that offer wider range of engagment but no real purpose. Story is meh. Its interesting and has its moments but I would not remember it a month from now.

Outside of the stealth or loud playstyle in the campaign the horde mode does offer enough content to keep you engaged. The multiplayer is not bad too but matches are a struggle to find.

In a nutshell, Eschalon is a standard 2D single-character fantasy western RPG. ("western RPG" here means "opposite of JRPG")
Eschalon is solid. It's not exemplary, it's not bad. It's the kind of game that would metascore in the 70-75 bracket, filled with games that are worth your time if you're a fan of the genre.
The story is cliche; save the world by finding the macguffins and slaying the big bad. That doesn't necessarily make it bad. It's not memorable, but it works.
For the most part, combat in Eschalon is a game of numbers and dice. I played a magick user, and for the first half of the game, all I had was a basic single-target spell. The outcome of a battle essentially boiled down to how many times I could cast it with what mana I had, how many turns it took the enemy to close to attack range (which is melee for most enemies), and how many hits both of us could survive. Later on, I got a few area-effect spells, which added a small layer of strategy, though numbers and dice were still the dominant factor.
The first half of the game was extremely tedious as a magick user. Mana regen is very slow to start, though you can build for quick regen after a few level ups if you eschew everything else. There is a rest function that causes time to pass more quickly, but it can still take as long as a minute to fill back up. Health regen works the same way, and I have to imagine it's just as tedious for melee-centered characters.
Basically, playing Eschalon Book 1 felt like playing a much, MUCH smaller Elder Scrolls game. That's just me though; your mileage may (and probably will) vary.
THE VERDICT: Eschalon is a solid RPG that will entertain an RPG fan for about 20 hours. It's not the best game out there, but it's not the worst either.

I`m 313 hours into Stellaris.  I haven´t completed it, but I believe I can give a pretty good impression of the game.
This review includes ALL the DLCs, up to and including Utopia.
Stellaris is one of those unique games where random♥♥♥♥♥♥happens so often that one game can feel like several new playthroughs. Over 300 hours into the game, I still often find brand new things happening  in single player and multiplayer modes.
You start with a single planet and a few people.  From there, you go off to take over the universe. You will encounter everything from space dragons, horrors of the void and pirates that will try to kill you. For that matter, half of the universe will also attempt to kill or devour you. The rest wanna make friends or simply breed you out of history.
Going into Stellaris, it is important to know that this is NOT a game you will finish in a day or a week.  It's a game where you should take your time and really learn and understand what is going on. It´s a game where every choice you make for your population affects the outcome of the game.
Reasearch, building, military and social aspects of your population are by your command. There are a million tools to reach your goal, so you get to pick whatever you want.
You wanna be a insane warmonger ? Sure, go ahead,
You wanna be a spiritual leader who believes in peace ? Sure, go ahead.
You wanna be the most tech-savvy scientist and have every population below you ? Sure, go ahead.
You wish to enslave the entire world and feel like a king with slaves ? Sure, go ahead.
You wanna be a complete asshat and purge people who disagree with you ? Sure, go ahead.
Stellaris lets you truly customize according to your whims and rule the universe as you like, which is great.
Design your own race, from appearance to values.
Design your own ships, with weapons, shields, and FTL drives.
Design your own planets with terraforming and much more.
Gameplay and graphics are amazing, complemented by a soundtrack that promotes relaxation on your journey into space.
Stellaris is strongly recommended for people who love complex, long-running GRTS games.

So, I finally had the chance to play through this completely, and finished it an hour or so ago...and I have to say I was VERY impressed. The first couple of times I tried (and got interrupted) I was a little confused because I found doors I just couldn't open, but never actually got the time to explore properly, but I'm glad now that I finally did.
Firstly, a warning of sorts, there's really not a whole lot going on in this game, the area you're able to explore is on the small side, there's not a lot of detail in anything, and there are no visible people ANYWHERE...that being said, what this dev did with what little he had at his disposal is well and truly worthy of praise.
The "lack" of detail in most of the surfaces is easily explained when a strong wind kicks up, blowing sand (albeit basic-graphics sand) everywhere, and we find out more about the island through various notes and remembered conversations.
The atmosphere and tension is far more palpable once you access beyond the few houses on the island, especially if you forget where the nearest charge-point for your flashlight is located...
In all, I'd be remiss to do anything less than highly recommend this game, it's something that everyone should play at least once.

Ok. I'm giving this one the thumbs down because there are better TW games on the market that you should buy.
Yes,  I have tons of hours on medieval II. Yes, I think it's a good game. But that's because I'm:
1. A MASSIVE TW FAN
2. A MASSIVE FAN OF THIS TIME PERIOD
So for me, I'm probably adding 3 extra points on the scale out of 10 than a regular RTS/G.S. gamer will.
Now then, I want to talk about a few things here:
1. AI is BAD
- - - 1.a. Campaign AI:
Sometimes factions will go to war with you just because. This is a problem because weak factions will go to war with you, and then they will ask for a peace treaty. You can really game the system because you can demand money as part of the peace treaty. Soooooooo a weak faction goes to war with you and then pays you money to stop the war. That's a problem.
Also, the game throws stacks at you without generals. That means those stacks always lose if you have a general.
- - - 1.b. Battle AI:
Battle AI is generally bad for a few reasons. [1] The game mixes unit types in armies, but some of the unit types are super weak. Specifically archers/siege units are very weak in field battles. But sometimes the AI will have a lot of ranged/siege units and just attack you even though it has no chance of winning. [2] The AI doesn't try and use the battle field terrain. You can easily manipulate the AI to give up the high ground. Also, chain routing is easy to do in this TW game, so the AI will almost always chain route if you flank properly.
2. Game doesn't make sense!
Say you play Scotland. You become an ally of England. England betrays your alliance and goes to war with you. The Pope gets MAD AT YOU because you're fighting England, which is a Christian faction. So the AI goes to war with you and then gets mad at you because you're at war!
3. Rebellions/enemy agents show up just because.
You can have a conetent city and a rebel army just shows up. You can have a territory that's mostly your faction's religion and an evil witch/priest will show up just because. If you set campaign difficulty to max difficulty this will happen. I understand that "very hard" should be very hard.... but to get rebellions when the territories are content just doesn't make sense and seems to be something they put into the game to justify the "very hard" difficulty setting.
4. You can't customize generals.
Generals will generate their own traits as they live. Sometimes the traits are useful, sometimes not so much. You don't really have control over any of this. You could make a general fight in a bunch of battles and he will naturally gain command, but you can't fine tune your generals to fit very specific roles.
5. Generals die quickly.
You progress through the years quickly. This is kinda sucks because you usually lose your faction leader in the early part of your game due to how old he is. Characters age quickly, so you can't get too attached to generals or use them for a very long period of time like you can in TW games like Shogun 2 - where you can use your faction leader for the entire game! This kind of makes sense because you start off in the Medieval era and your late game units are early rifle units, so it would make sense for you to burn through a few generations before you got to the late game.
6. Ranged units are usually not good (not including rifles).
Archers are either useful or terrible. They're useful for using fire arrows as a moral shock/setting siege engines on fire. But, they do almost no damage to enemy units. So you're always better off trying to flank an enemy army and causing it to route rather than use ranked units. In defense, a few ranged units are OK, but overall archers just aren't that great in this version of TW with the exception of a few.
If Medieval II is on sale, yeah - give it a try. But if you're interested in TW and want a solid game I highly recommend Shogun 2. The AI is good, the combat is good, and the game is frequently on sale, as well as FOTS.
Overall, I love Medieval II, but there are so many other better, more polished, modern Total War games you can buy and enjoy. I only recommend this game to people who are old time Total war fans like myself, or if you want to visit an older title.

This is a suprisingly fun mix of Navy Fields, World of Warships and World of Tanks. Taking influences from all of them and turning them into an interesting and entertaining F2P title.
After playing a few hours I personally start to prefer it over WoWS; it features a more demanding gunnery with maneuvering and aim-time having more influence on spread of a volley than in WoWs, also you get manual control over your secondaries and heavy AAA which I personaly prefer. While the ranges are 'shorter' when you go by the range displayed, they feel a lot longer than in WoWs right from the start thanks to the different scale of the ships themselves and the battlefield.
Also, Torpedos in this game actually have arming distances.
The game also expands the battlefield with another class of vessels, submarines are playable and introduce a new threat to BBs and lone carriers while expanding the duty of DDs and CLs to submarine warfare.
It's of course not without flaws, It is certainly a bit uglier than WoWs though it easily beats NF, but that's not really a challenge (not talking about NF2, nobody talks about NF2). There are only NA servers available, so I have to play with a rather high ping of 120 to 200 from central europe. And the UI is not the cleanest design around.
That said, it's free. So if you're interested in a (F2P) naval arcade combat game, just download it and sink a few ships to see if it fits you and judge yourself if you like it more than its competitors or not.

My first impressions (coming from other Paradox games like EU-IV and CK2):
#1: The UI is somewhat messy. Anything new takes time to learn, but in this case I feel like there are genuine issues in Stellaris. After CK2, Paradox seemed to realize that the UI they put out is sometimes needlessly complex or even sometimes redudant in sections. Hence, EU-IV did a decent job of presenting tons of info in a simple manner, and HoI-IV, whatever its other issues, made info extremely easy to get at. Then Stellaris comes along and throws info at me from every which direction, sometimes without sufficient tool-tips (and yes, I left the beginner's stuff on and didn't skip over it). Again, part of it is just me being new, but the default map screen, the way subscreens are accessed, etc., is all a bit clunkier than the last couple games.
#2: Surprisingly, then, I have to admit: the screens for setting up the game and choosing universe size and so on, are actually perfect. I can choose my empire or build a new one; if I build a new empire, I can elect to have it be forbidden from being played by the CPU; I can choose the percentage of planets that will be habitable. The options are concise, include anything I could think of that really matters that much. For one of the few games Paradox has done that has procedural generation for elements, I'm pleasantly surprised that they nailed it straight out of the gates as far as settings.
#3: Early game has a lot to do, but is strangely slow. Probably just me, but I'm used to immediately having enemy countries at my door, or the Spanish Civil War to send a Panzer or two at in order to intervene. It took a decent chunk of time just to spot any other factions, though this could be luck-of-the-draw for my first game.
#4: I just got this on sale, and picked up all content-adding DLC along with it. So keep in mind that my reaction is based on everything, not just the vanilla game.

(Before I get going, I'll say that Book 2 is much improved and although I'm only a few hours in, I can probably recommend Book 2. Writing is more polished, graphics feel fresher, and controls feel more responsive. Book 1 isn't necessary to play or understand the story of Book 2.)
Slow paced and feels more like a shallow copy of old school CRPGs (hey, that *looks old-fashioned*, or, nobody does *that* in RPGs anymore, let's put that into Eschalon) rather than capturing the deep magic that made old school CRPGs worth reviving (as in "why did they do that, and does it still make sense? If so, let's put it in and modernize it just a bit"). Don't get me wrong, I like turn-based (Western) CRPGs, love Spiderweb Games (Exile through Avadon even), and I even fire up one of the top roguelikes now and then (Nethack, ADOM, dwarf fortress, Cataclysm DDA, etc.), and Eschalon Book 1 falls flat by comparison. I've played Ultima 4-8, Wasteland, Fallout 1-2, Baldur's Gate, Arcanum, and I've probably played other awesome turn-based overhead CRPGs that I can't remember. I'm sure I've played some clunkers too, but I felt I had to put up this negative review if only b/c I cannot figure out why so many people seem to like this game enough to recommend others play it--the hype for this game, from "pro" reviews and players, makes me wonder how many of those even played a quarter of the games I listed up top.
Eschalon Book 1 is a passable timesink, but do yourself a favor and fire up an actual classic or one of the better old-school-style titles this side of 1999. Even if it's cheap, there's still your time to consider--a playthrough takes about 20-40 hours depending on how OCD you get on doing quests and leveling up, and much of that will be spent slowly walking your single toon around obstacles since there's no click-move.
As for the plot, it's pretty straightforward w/o any real interesting twists, the writing is passable, but there's no real drama, tension, or even humor. There's *some* sure, but most of it is rather flat and just something to check the box.
Now, nobody ever came out and said this was a "love letter" to old-school CRPGs, but much of the marketing kept hyping up it's old-school-ness. To that I respond: 1) actual old CRPGs did it better, 2) some of those old CRPGs are still playable now, 3) newer CRPGs in old-school-style have also done it better.
If you read this and still played the game, no problem, even if you found you liked it enough to at least *want* to play it *a second time* (how many Yes-recommenders honestly think they'd *want* to play a second time? That's not even *actually* playing it twice, but just *thinking* about it?). I'm not saying I know all for everybody. If you played it and didn't like it, then at least know you've not gone crazy considering how many reviews recommend it. If you have yet to play it, seriously, track down and play the other names I've dropped first, then maybe you can at least be so busy putting in the hours into those that you won't even have to think about Eschalon.

Be warned! If you're a fan of casual RPGs, this one is not for you. It's an epic quest of XP grinding, min-maxing and filling your inventory with alchemical ingerients. Therefore I'm going to give this one a thumbs down.
There's some pen-and-paper retro charm to Eschalon that makes it worthwhile to people who really love turn based and number-driven adventures with no dedicated run buttons. You have to rest for eight hours to regain mana in order to kill a single bumble bee. If that's your thing, who am I to judge?
Get out now, before you are sucked into the endless hours of fun and frustration that...too late. If you've read this far you are probably going to spend 200+ hours playing this game.

Imagine Minecraft and Terraria's crafting system, with the roguelike elements of Rogue Legacy, and Risk of Rain's area to area placement of random generation. The graphics are similar to Castle Crashers and
, because of the pixel art style its derived from.
Your objective is simple, survive at least 20 districts in, and kill the end boss, all while leveling with random drops and level stat progression.
There are hats, which change subtle ways you can play, which can be unlocked, along with races which have different gains in those stat areas. Some are more Dex based for archery, some are more towards magic, while others deal in strength.
There are also companions you can earn, which can help you in your quest. All of these have to be unlocked, and some are 100% chances to gain, others are 20%. You may have to run more than a few times to get everything.
It's a great game, though it does have a few issues, but they're pretty minor. Such as being unable to 'Play Again!' after a loss in Multiplayer, which results in a black screen for those connected to the host sometimes. As well as being able to take advantage of the 1HP revive. Though these are minor, if you have patience to accept it.
Once you get the hang of the crafting system, the game gets really fun. However, this game is best played with friends.
I love this game and it is a good way to pass the time.

This game is truly cute. I love it to bits. Tiny bits if i am going to be honest here because that is what i do in this game. I go in and love them to bits.
Now lets be serious. This game is a roguelike 2D Platform Sidescroller and it truly makes itself look amazing. The overall game plays itself very easily and the controlls are just as easy as the game is. But dont think the game is actually easy. The game is just like any other Roguelike game very hard. The game can not only be hard but also nearly impossible at times. Or atleast that is how it seems.
In the game you will not get anything. Everything depends on your class and Perks. Well actually it depends only on your playstyle since even with the most amazing perks you will die if you are not good at the game. That means that in the end you can die if you cannot dodge a certain attack or enemy. And if you people know what bullethell means then you know exactly what can come at you.
The game has unlockables but you have to do certain things to unlock them. You have to even cheat for one of the unlocks but i am not going to tell you how. The hint is out and now its your thing to find it out. There are three different types of unlockables. Class | Equipment | Pet.
The Classunlocks give you different Skins and different Items to start. The Equipmentunlocks give you Hats that give you certain attributs and effects. With one hat you might be able to jump higher or to run faster. With the next one you are able to get more from Mining rocks and ore. The Petunlocks give you Pets. Every Pet has a different effect and remains as a neutral companion who grants you his powers. One pet may grant you Health as you complete a level. The next pet may grant you extra stats up while leveling up.
But how do you get all of this? By playing the game a whole lot. And by completing it too. And that is no easy task. If you people are familar with Terraria then you know what the infamous "Wall of Flesh" is. The same Enemy waits for you as Endboss with one really big twist. The Level ends at a certain point and is just as long as the other levels. So it is up to you and your playstyle if you live or die.
But no matter how frustrating this game was for me i can only recommend this game. It is cute and just amazing. I had a lot of fun playing it even though i am not playing it anymore.

I do not know what I can say about this game, other than it being a masterpiece. I have to say that this is one of the best games I have ever played. Everything in it was just so good: the gameplay, the story and the setting, the characters etc, but the game did have some performance issues.
All of the characters were crafted pretty well but they did have some certain noticeable tropes, for example: 2B is the serious character while 9S is a more childish and loose character, even though these tropes were so obvious the characters were still pretty interesting and built up pretty well throughout the story. There are some characters which seem like they are made for comedic relief but really have a deep side story, example (Emil). Overall the characters in this game were great
The story in this game is amazing, it has a series of really unexpected plot twists and amazing moments that I will remember for a long time. I think that the setting for this game was also a bit radical being a set a very long time in the future with androids everywhere and a giant space station, but on the ground everything seemed pretty old which was a pretty weird design decision and I liked it, this whole artstyle actually tied in with the old games so there was a good reason to choose such a different look for the game. The whole backstory of this game was also pretty amazing, you didn't really need to play the old games to get the main part of the story but if you wanted to go deeper and find out more you would have to refer to the old games like Nier: Gestalt. To be honest I found myself to be really invested in the storyline as it was pretty different from anything I have played.
There are some really nice and original gameplay mechanics in it as well like being able to take off your HUD to make space for upgrades, the whole upgrade system in the game was really interesting and well crafted, I think that it was a very good choice to experiment with it and not make the upgrade system as basic as skill points, the upgrade system could also help you find entirely new moves which was pretty cool. The weapon upgrade system was pretty simple which isn't a bad thing, it didn't need to be any harder. The fighting in the game wasn't that satisfying but it was fine, the actual moves that you can do were at first pretty basic with only having a heavy and a light attack but as you play and combine the moves together you can find some combos that the game did not tell you about. I think that one good choice in this game was how you could equip the weapons because it forced you to think about what do you want on the heavy attack and on the light attack, do you want a small sword with a heavy attack, or a large sword with a heavy attack? There was also quite a lot of weapons that you could find around the world and buy from stores which would benefit you a lot as you go on.
The performance issues did not even bother me since I was so invested into the game and they really weren't that bad, the only big problem that happened to me was 30fps lock on cutscenes (disgusting) and the low fps ingame. Having a pretty beefy computer I would expect this game to run better, but for me it wasn't really that big of a problem.
To summarise this game, I have to say that is very well made with a good story, characters, setting and gameplay elements, but this game was limited by it's performance issues. Overall this game was really one of the best games I have ever played and an actual masterpiece. This was definitely one of the best games I have ever played on one of the best games of 2017. I would have to give this game at least a 9/10 and to quote Jim Sterling - "I history forgets this game, then ♥♥♥♥ history."

Welp, finally decided to write a review for this masterpiece of a game after completing 100% achievements and 70 hours of in-game time.
Firstly, do not be fooled by the fanservice in NieR: Automata. NieR: Automata's story is probably one of the most heart wrenching stories in a RPG/JRPG in years, it hits you like a truck especially hard in the feels if you like I, have played the original NieR. The Story is broken into 3 parts, the first two leading to endings A and B, and the third leading to C,D & E after you've completed the first four. These are just the 5 main endings of the 26 possible. I wholly recommend playing through the game a second or third time even after completing the 5 main endings, as it'll really open your eyes to everything happening around you, and that everything is interconnected to one another in which you may miss if you only played the game through one time.
The story, coupled with the amazing atmosphere that is woven in from the smooth fluid transition from a thirdperson view to a sidescroller view, to even topdown, coupled with very well done bullet hell gameplay and sequences, truly makes NieR:Automata a wonderful masterpiece.
The soundtrack. The soundtrack is amazing. The amount of emotions captured in the vocals as well as the depth it adds to the atmosphere, has really contributed to the emotional impact in many portions of the story. it's almost impossible to describe how great the soundtrack is with mere words. Major props to Keiichi Okabe and Emi Evans.

The game features a solid career mode, where you create a player from scratch and work your way to stardom in the NBA. That character can then be taken to MyPark to face off against other players online (more on that later).
Another gem is MyGM/League. As you'd expect, you manage a team to a championship, taking care of all the minutia between games.
My personal favorite mode is MyTeam. In this mode you build a squad of current and/or former NBA players by collecting their cards. Then test your squad in weekly challenges or face off against historic teams to unlock various rewards. MyTeam also offers competetive online modes, but this is where the issues arise...
NBA 2k17's multiplayer is completely broken on PC. Cheaters are rampant and go unchecked by 2k. I litterally can't play the MyTeam Online modes because hackers crash the game before it even starts. Somehow crashing the game gives them a W and me a L while using up my contracts. Like I said, it's an unplayable mess. From what I understand the console versions of the game are mostly fine, so I guess 2k just doesn't care about the PC community. They already got our money...so GG.
tl;dr - If you're only interested in singleplayer, this game is a ton of fun. Multiplayer? I wouldn't expect 2K to fix anything at this point. So either buy a console or you're wasting your money.

With enjoyable game-play, decent graphics, and strong co-operative potential to draw from, Ghost Recon Future Soldier should have been a fantastic game, and the console version is. Unfortunately, Ubisoft has proven once more to care very little for their PC fan base by releasing a game so riddled with bugs, that a huge portion of the player base cannot even play the game, which is just an example of blatant laziness on the part of the developers.
No matter that it is based on an extremely successful franchise and could otherwise be a brilliant game, using the controls is unbearable, let alone all of the left over icons from the Xbox version, inclusion of mouse acceleration and the lack of any real customisation menus. This makes it difficult to want to be able to progress through the game regardless of how good the story or multi-player could be.
The developers tried their hardest to make it seem like this game is not on rails, but it is. You have operational freedom when you’re in designated combat areas but always have to follow their lead. When you’re in camouflage, you may never run for extended periods without losing the use of the camouflage, however, your team mates may run, gun and dance while their camouflage is still active and stays active. Furthermore, your team mates are either super heroes or idiots, either spotting and killing adversaries before you ever do so, or standing around like idiots while you’re bleeding out at their feet. The ability to customise your weapons is a stand-out feature; however it fails to carry the game.
While it looks pretty and sounds good, it doesn’t make the game; playability and usability do. You’d be glad if you got this game for free, or if you must have it, wait for it to reach the bargain bin.

In response to the recent crap about this game being abandoned:
Now I have been hearing a lot of crap about how this game has been abandoned and how you “Should not buy it until its finished.” Screw those guys. They have NOT played it enough. I mean the guys have not even played 5 hours. So yes this game has not been updated since 9/20/2015, but if you take a honest look at what they have here its a near complete game. The only update it may need are a couple of bug fixes to things not even game breaking. I mean its not like cube world where there is nothing and might be abandoned. Cube world is boring and abandoned. This game is fun and might be abandoned. This game still has new things to throw at me and I have played 42 hours so far and thinking I've seen everything but then I made a new play through and boom I've seen a dungeon layout that I've never seen before. I even saw some treasure rooms and I'm like “Since when did delver have treasure rooms?” Put this game on your wish list and buy it when its on sale. This game is worth it.
Now time to my actual review
This game is a throwback to how games used to be. Before story was added. Before you needed to know enough statistics you might as well get a fricken degree in the stuff. I thinking of YOU pokemon, I love you but my gosh your competitive play is just full of maths. Literally you wake up at a camp and need talk to some guys and walk into a door and boom your in the game. Your goal? Get to the end of the dungeon, grab the orb and get back to the start. Sounds easy right? Hah! Nope! As soon as you grab the orb, the quiet peacefull dungeon run you had on the way down, which I must say isn't very hard but just engaging enough to keep playing but at the same time punishes your mistakes, is now a absolute hell hole where you just want to survive the trek up. I make sounds of terror that I have never made before on my way up. If your an angry person, this game may not be for you just for this part. My gosh I love it. As soon as you grab the orb you see why this game is called rouge like.
I rate this game 10/10 yes I really do, I don't care if its abandoned or not this is a good game.
If you don't want to buy it now put it on your wish list and remember it exists because you have no excuse to not buy this game when its on sale. This is one of the best Indie games I've played and deserves more credit.

This game you spend the entire 40 minutes it takes to finish, wandering by yourself around a small empty island reading books and looking at objects that make you read. Counterstrike is a game that slowly ravages and pulverizes your soul each and every time you play it.

Within a month -
Within a week -
