With lots of gratuitous panty shots.
Alternate review:
Platinum Games makes a JRPG.  Except it's the Platinum Games that made Korra and Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles, not the Platinum Games that made Bayonetta/Vanquish/Metal Gear Rising.
Combat is *not* deep or nuanced, devolving into button mashing with no finesse required (unlike Bayonetta), the camera is occasionally finnicky, blocking the action (unlike Metal Gear Rising), the controls aren't precise and instinctive (unlike Vanquish), the open world is rather bland, lacking imagination (unlike ... pretty much all their other games)  ... and the story is  ... well, it's a typical JRPG-esque storyline  (and no, that's not a compliment)
However, I'm still going to give this game a recommendation because it's still super stylish with high production values, and if I don't, a bunch of whiny JRPG fans are going to e-mail bomb me.  (...and gratuitous panty shots)

Delver is a 3D rogue-like game with randomly generating dungeons, and a randomly generated starting inventory each time you start a new game, making each playthrough fairly unique.
Hopefully, future update will make the game a bit longer, as finishing it (without counting the failed tries) can easily be done in just a few minutes.
However, I did have quite a lot of fun in this game, discovering new dungeons and loot every time I played.
Also, this game has a texture pack by Sphax already, which gives me hopes for future mods or even more texture packs (hopefully though, these ones will be free...).
Overall, this is a fun and good game if you don't wanna get involved for countless hours of playing. A new game of Delver is always fun to play, and with the high amount of updates, there are lots of new things to discover.

Guys 'n gals, buy this game. Srsly. I thoroughly enjoy Delver and I own it on Android as well. The mobile version is a bit behind the PC/Mac version, but definitely worth it. Let's be honest about rogue-likes: they're a dime a dozen. So many rogue wannabes on all platforms. So that begs the question: What makes Delver stand out? I'll sum it up in a short list.
1. Atmosphere - music, environment, decoration, ambiance. They nailed it.
2. Mechanics - the gameplay is super simple but somehow I don't feel it's repetetive.
3. Monster variety - See #2; the variety of monster types and attacks keeps combat feeling fresh.
4. Inventory/RPG aspects - The inventory is simple but covers all the bases. Easy-peasy, but deep eough now that they have rings, amulets, off-hand (shield, candle, etc.)
That's my $.02. This game is a blast. Delver has improved upon the basic RPG/rogue elements, but not so much as to lose the heart and soul of the genre.
Highly recommended.

In my opinion the best of the Total War series. Especially the interaction with the pope makes you think a bit more about every move you make. For me, the best part is the historical fantasies you can enjoy, in small things like conquering the British Isles with Scotland (Bloody Englishmen!) or on larger scales, like creating the resurgence of the dying Byzantine Empire.
The AI is not perfect, especially in the real time battles, and the influences of popes, imams, crusades and jihads does leave the orthodox with a less interesting experience. Orthodox popes did exist at that time, so it seems like a missed opportunity.
Overall though, many issues can be solved through the great modding scene. In the end, this is just one of those games you want to play for a quick ten turns, only to end up 5 hours and 120 turns later, reigning over the half of Europe and in battle with the other half.

I don't quite know what to make of this game. Tactically, the game is brilliant, as usual for Total War. The battles are majestic and make sense for the most part, and you actually do have to use what would amount to standard medieval tactics to win these engagements. On the strategic level, this game is horrible. The AI, no matter what difficulty setting you have it turned to, seems to be permanently set to 'Syphilitic Bipolar Nero.' What makes the AI in this game so hard to beat on the campaign map is that it is utterly unpredictable. For example, in one campaign I was the only faction to join and successfully complete the Crusade the Pope called for. I built numerous churches and used a whole lot of missionaries to bludgeon my faith into nearby territories like a bunch of Jehova's Witnesses on crack/cocaine. What did this get me? I was excomunicated and wiped off the map by less pious kingdoms. Other factions will attack for no reason, refuse to settle a conflict EVEN THOUGH they are about to be wiped out, and just generally behave like 5-year olds. There are better medieval strategy games than this. 4/10.

I'm not sure how I ended up with this game, I must have bought it a long time ago. While surfing my library I happened to see it and gave it a try. I gotta say, I really love it.
It's probably my favorite twin stick shooter. Too many games just use arena or survival formats, this one has a plot, objectives and secrets a la Doom style. The graphics are also pretty great in my opinion for a game of this type.
Two things I especially love about this game is that #1: There is a lot of variety. Almost every level introduces a new enemy, sometimes a new mechanic or a new weapon, which leads me to #2: None of the guns seem redundant. Every weapon is useful in certain situations. You're not gonna upgrade the heck out of one gun and use it the entire game, you'll be switching on the fly. Upgrades themselves are great too. Overall, I bought it at 4.90 USD and I'd say it was worth it, let alone now on sale for under a dollar.
Also there is multiplayer, I haven't tried it yet so I can't comment on that.
The only con's I can think of is that (one time for me) you can get stuck between objects and get trapped. Again, it happened once for me so it might have been a one time thing. Either way my autosave brought me back a whole five minutes so no big deal. Second is that flares seem a bit OP and you get a ton of them, but that's my opinion, plus I'm playing on normal and not hard. Third... lol the voice acting is horrendous. The main character does an okay job, but every NPC is laughably bad.
PS: Almost forgot to mention, the sounds effects are awesome. From the gunshots and explosions to the various creatures moans and screams and explosive gory deaths. At .50 you'd be silly not to pick this up. Even if you, for some reason, don't like it... it's .49 cents...

Yes, it's apparently possible to beat level 7 if you singlemindedly devote your time and attention to it for hours. But I had to ask myself, "is it even really worth it? For a game like NO THING?" and the immediate answer that came to mind was "absolutely not".
Dev: you have a shallow yet aestheticky game on your hands, there's no need to make it this difficult just for street cred. Your game doesn't have enough going for it to warrant making any of the levels as unforgiving as level 7. You're being precocious, I get it, but you can stop now.

I don't fully dislike the game, but i'm not enamored by it either way. Just like many, many, many other users, i thought the game would be similar to Hotline Miami, but with a stealth element added to it and far wittier. Well, i was wrong.
The good:
- Pretty visuals, it's generic pixel art, but i really like it,  especially the colour espectrum, that neon aesthetic.
- The traps can be very fun, they're what actually made the game interesting for me.
- Everytime you restart a map, it will have different trap combinations, however this can be a double edged sword: you can get a very good combo or a totally useless one.
- Sometimes people can blame eachother and they get arrested instead of you, don't know how it exactly gets triggered but it's a pretty cool mechanic. Some maps have pre-scripted events in them, like a robbery in the casino level.
The bad:
-  You move very slowly,party goers are slower than you until they start panicking. Can you sprint? yes, you can... it's useless 99% of the time.
- The bouncers randomly chase you, at first i thought they would only beat you up if you tried to sneak into a VIP area so to speak, but on later levels they're guarding the entire map apparently.
- The soundtrack can get on your nerves due to the repetitiveness of it.
- No proper tutorial, there are newspaper that act as hints but they're random and most of the time aren't actually useful or related to the level you're playing.
- There's no consistency in difficulty.
- If you end up using all the traps/have a bad trap combo, you will have to kill the party goers one by one, and it can be tedious and boring.
- The character rooster isn't really great. All of them have pros and cons, but the cons far outweight the pros, so you're better off just sticking with the default character.
- The story is very weak and has a twist that you can see coming pretty easily + atrocious voice acting.
In short: it's a fun game in short bursts, it's not a good stealth game. It's nothing like Hotline Miami aside from the neon pixel aesthetic.

I really wanted to like this game,  but honestly I just was bored to tears almost the whole time.  It could have been great, and I initally bought it because it seemed like an entertainingly over-the-top riff on sneaky ultraviolence.
Ultimately though, it feels more like a brainless retread of bad Newgrounds game.  The art is neat, the music isn't bad, but the gameplay is dull with braindead AI. I wanted a game that felt like a "♥♥♥♥ it" playthrough of a Hitman level, or a more sneaky Hotline Miami.  It wasn't.
It's really CLOSE to being a fun game.  There is humor in some of the available methods of murder in the game.  Party Hard revels in cartoonish ultraviolence, but doesn't make the actual violence visceral or interactive.  Hit use, watch red pixels, repeat until dead or new level opens up.  Some of the unlockable characters add fun twists to the base formula, but it's really not enough to justify the price.  The best moments in the game, which felt too few and far between, was causing cascading mayhem and making the NPCs do my work for me.  More of that, and more variety in the mayhem the player can cause, would be welcome.  I wouldn't recommend this game, but if the developer manages to meaningfully improve the game in Party Hard 2, that might be worth it.

I've been playing WildStar since about 3 months before it went F2P. This game has excellent graphics, humour (reminiscent of Ratchet and Clank), AMAZING music which really contributes to the atmosphere and best of all is the outstanding combat.
I'm a huge fan of WoW and the original Guild Wars but I think the combat in Wildstar easily topples those. The combat works on telegraphs, which are markers on the ground that display where exactly the attack will hit (the range, width of cone etc.). Without having to tab target different enemies all the time, aim becomes more important which massively lends to skill rather than who can hit tab the fastest and also opens every attack up to become AoE. Another decision that I love is only having one action bar. In Guild Wars you chose 8 skills out of everything available to you which would essentially be your build. WildStar is much the same, and so you don't need a 40 button mouse and macro filled £100 keyboard to easily access every skill, and the skill cap comes more from choosing skills that work in a cohesive manner, rather than being able to quickly access a skill that you might use every 4 hours very situationally.
The graphics on the game are rich and detailed. Closest comparison is probably to WoW but with a lot more character and they really help to bring Nexus to life. The music is absolutely my favourite thing though, from grinding techno to sweeping orchestral music, I think a good deal of budget was plowed into the music because it's always epic and never manages to feel out of place as you adventure round the planet.
If I was scoring WildStar I'd give it a solid 9/10. I think it more than holds it's own among other MMOs and I really struggle to see why it hasn't truly taken off, especially when compared to the likes of FFXIV, WoW and GW2. As it's now F2P and available on Steam there's no reason to not try it but be careful, the world of Nexus might just have you so engrossed that you too wind up passionately expressing your love for the game!

100% cool.
Not the overused copyandpastenobodycaresshit-cool. More the deeplyimpressedbypureawesomeness-cool that you rarely use for describing something because of its fresh style, feeling or mindchanging character. Let's be honest: Not everything can be cool and not everything cool can be cool for everybody. You need a special kind of taste for visuals and music as well as an eager fighting spirit to be able to enjoy NO THING. Personally I was immediately hooked by watching the trailer that shows what the game is - left and right at the left and right time, pure adrenaline and finest vaporwave art.
NO THING will take you on an immersive trip, the synergy of graphics, voice and tunes is exceptional, the gameplay feels super smooth and the addictive restartitoverandoveragain-engine runs with the beginning of the first minute. Did somebody already mention that this game ist hard? Yes, this person was right. NO THING makes no bones about the fact that it is very unforgiving, extremely repetitive and demanding in every aspect (I made it only to Level 4 of 10 so far). If you can deal with that, I can tell you NO THING is a very good small game for a reasonable price.
To make it short: If you like the trailer - buy the game. And consider buying the soundtrack as well.
